title: PatientSummary
description: Shape contract for the patient-summary pass: three sets extracted from a patient's whole record, not from one note. Unlike the vital-signs pass — which transcribes numbers out of a single document — this reads many notes assembled into one message under the rule in [clinical.summaryAssembly], and what it returns is prose a clinician would recognise rather than figures a scorer can compare exactly.

x-notes.whyArraysNotObjects: A summary is set extraction. There is no fixed slot list to fill and no way to know in advance how many antecedents a patient has, so the contract is three bounded arrays rather than nine nullable properties. That difference is what makes this task worth having in the pack: it exercises the schema shape the vital-signs task cannot, and it is the shape that goes wrong in a way a grammar makes worse rather than better.
x-notes.maxItems: LOAD-BEARING, and the reason this file needs care the vital-signs schema does not. A GBNF grammar cannot emit EOS while an array is open, so the model must reach the closing bracket and an UNBOUNDED array leaves it no way to stop. Measured on a sibling pack: an unbounded extraction array ran to 3483 tokens of repeated items before hitting the token cap.
x-notes.uniqueItems: Also load-bearing, and enforced rather than accepted-and-ignored by llama.cpp b10333. With maxItems alone a model pads to the cap with duplicates instead of terminating: a sibling trial produced 40 items of which 38 were the same string, in 80 seconds; adding uniqueItems returned 2 distinct items in 7. CAVEAT: uniqueness is exact string equality, so 'hypertension' and 'hypertension since 2019' are both legal. Near-miss deduplication is not something a grammar can do, and the prompt asks for it instead.
x-notes.cap20: 20 per field, read by anyone reading this pack so no runtime invents its own. Not lower: a multimorbid patient across a dozen notes genuinely carries more than a handful of problems, and a cap that truncates real findings is a worse failure than padding — it is invisible, where padding is obvious. Re-derive from traces before tightening it.
x-notes.noNulls: Every property is REQUIRED and every one is an array. The single way to say a section is empty is `[]`. Two spellings — `null` and `[]` — would split the eval's counts across both and make item recall unreadable, which is the same argument the vital-signs schema makes for the opposite shape: there, one way to say absent is `null`; here, it is the empty array. What matters is that there is exactly one.
x-notes.maxTokensIsAConsequence: The caller's max_tokens must sit above three arrays × 20 items × a line's worth of tokens, or a legal maximal response truncates mid-array and every long summary becomes a parse failure. See [sampling.patient_summary] in models.default.toml: the cap is a backstop, not a budget.

history.description: Ongoing or previous problems the record establishes: chronic conditions, resolved episodes worth carrying forward, relevant surgery. NOT today's examination findings, not a problem the record attributes to a relative, and never a negation the notes make.

usual_medication.description: What the patient takes on an ongoing basis, with the dose where a note gives one. A drug the record stops does not belong here, and neither does a one-off dose given during an encounter.

pending.description: Investigations, results and follow-up the record leaves outstanding. Something a later note reports as done or received is no longer pending, which is the discriminator this field exists for.
